chunks: And from him, from Abū ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Ayyūb al-Makkī, from ʿAlī ibn Asbāṭ, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Bukayr, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said:
“There is no harm in a Muslim woman praying while there is no head-covering upon her head.”

So it is possible that what is intended by these two reports is young girls among women, not adult women, because it is permissible for them to pray without a head-covering. It is also possible that this was only permitted for them in a state in which they were unable and incapable of obtaining a head-covering; then, in that case, it is permissible for them to pray without a head-covering. It is also possible that what is intended by his statement, “she prays without a head-covering,” is when she has upon her a garment that covers her from her head to her feet. As for the second hadith, there is no mention in it of a free woman; rather, it only includes mention of the Muslim woman, and it is possible that what is intended by that is a bondwoman, because the bondwoman is not obligated to wear a head-covering according to what we have mentioned, and this further clarifies it.

key_terms.الصَّغِيرَةَ: a young girl who has not reached legal adulthood
key_terms.الْبَالِغَاتِ: adult women who have reached legal maturity
key_terms.الْحُرَّةِ: a free woman, as distinct from a bondwoman in legal rulings
key_terms.الْمَرْأَةُ الْمُسْلِمَةُ: a Muslim woman mentioned in the report under legal discussion
key_terms.ثَوْبٌ: a garment that may serve as covering in prayer
key_terms.قِنَاعٌ: a head-covering worn by a woman in the context of salat

ai.seo_question: When is it permissible for a Muslim woman to pray without a head-covering according to this hadith discussion?
ai.summary: This passage discusses the legal implications of a report permitting a Muslim woman to pray without a head-covering. It presents possible reconciliations, including that the ruling may apply to young girls, to cases of inability, to full-body covering by another garment, or to a bondwoman rather than a free woman.
